title: Direct IgG epitope mapping on bacterial AB toxins by cryo-EM
protocol: Extract total RNA from hybridoma cells using the RNeasy mini kit.
Perform cDNA synthesis using the iScript cDNA synthesis system with mouse IgG reverse transcription primers.
Mix the universal forward PCR primer with cDNA template for amplification of antibody variable regions.
Perform the first stage of PCR reaction using reverse PCR primers specific to the antibody chain.
Run 1% agarose gel electrophoresis to visualize amplicons from the first-stage PCR.
Extract DNA fragments between 550–600 base pairs from the agarose gel using QIAEX II DNA Extraction Kit.
Set up the second-stage PCR reaction using extracted DNA as template.
Prepare pET28a+ vector amplicon using primer pair specific for light and heavy chains.
Gibson-assemble the PCR amplicons with the prepared pET28a+ vector to form circular plasmid.
Transform the Gibson-assembled circular plasmid into E. coli DH5α cells.
Isolate a single colony from the transformed bacteria.
Sanger-sequence the isolated plasmid using T7 promoter or terminator primer.
Centrifuge cell culture supernatants for 15 min at approximately 6,000 × g at 4°C using JLA8.1 rotor.
Filter cleared hybridoma supernatants through 0.2 μm cellulose acetate filters.
Pack protein G resins in a 25 mL gravity plastic column and equilibrate by flowing 20 ml of binding buffer (20 mM sodium phosphate buffer, pH 7.0).
Submit cleared hybridoma supernatants to the prepared Protein G resin three times.
Wash antibody-bound resins with 25–50 ml of binding buffer.
Elute bound antibodies using 10 ml of elution buffer (0.1 M glycine-HCl, pH 2.7) into a conical tube containing 1 ml of equilibration buffer (1 M Tris-HCl, pH 8.0).
Monitor purity and yield of purified antibodies via 15% SDS-PAGE.
Divide purified antibodies in 50 μl aliquots and store at -80°C until use.
Concentrate purified mAbs to 20 mg/mL in 0.1 mL of buffer containing 20 mM sodium phosphate, pH 7.0, and 10 mM EDTA.
Mix 250 μL of equilibrated immobilized Papain with 1 mL of concentrated mAbs and incubate for at least 16 h at 37°C.
Elute the digested mAb samples in a buffer containing 10 mM Tris-HCl, pH 7.5.
Separate the Fab from uncut mAbs and Fc using a Superdex 75 10/300 Increase column with a buffer containing 10 mM Tris-HCl, pH 7.5 at a constant flow of 0.5 mL/min.
Transform the typhoid toxin plasmid in E. coli BL21(DE3) competent cells.
Inoculate a single colony in 10 mL of LB and culture at 37°C for at least 18 hours.
Transfer 5 mL of the overnight culture into 50 mL of LB in a baffled flask and culture at 37°C, 200 rpm for 3 hours.
When OD600 reaches 0.5, change to 28°C and 130 rpm.
After 30 minutes, add IPTG (final concentration 125 μM) to each culture.
Incubate the cultures at 28°C overnight with stirring.
Harvest bacterial cells by centrifuging at 5000 × g for 15 min at 4°C.
Pour off the supernatant into an empty flask and bleach (10% v/v).
Scoop out the pellet and combine up to two flasks' worth of pellets into a single 50 mL tube.
Store the pellet at −80°C if desired.
Add 25 mL of buffer A to a 50 mL conical tube containing bacterial pellets from up to 2 L culture.
Vortex the mixture to resuspend the bacteria.
Add a protease inhibitor cocktail solution (final, 1x), 2 mg/mL lysozyme, and 40 μg/mL DNAse I to the tube.
Invert the tube several times to mix thoroughly.
Subject the bacteria solution to three repeats of freeze-thaw in liquid nitrogen.
Lyse the cells using a 200-Watt ultrasonic homogenizer with a 1/8” probe (VWR) for 4 min using ‘Time – Pulse’ setup at 75% power, with 20 sec-on and 20 sec-off intervals.
Clarify the lysate by centrifugation for 30 min at 18,000 × g at 4°C.
Load the clarified lysate onto 10 mL of Ni-NTA equilibrated with buffer A.
Wash the column with 100 mL of buffer A.
Elute the protein with 50 mL of buffer B and collect 7 mL fractions.
Combine elute fractions containing desired protein.
Concentrate the combined fractions using Amicon columns, 30 kDa cutoff (ThermoFisher) until the volume reaches less than 5 mL.
Add 45 mL of buffer C to a 50 mL conical tube and up to 5 mL of concentrated Ni-IMAC eluate to lower the pH and salt level.
Load the protein solution onto a 5 mL SP HiTrap column equilibrated with buffer C.
Connect the column to the AKTA system.
Run the ‘Toxin SP – Opt’ program: Equilibrate AKTA A-line with buffer C, B-line with buffer D.
Set a flow rate of 1 mL/min.
Fractionate at 1 mL intervals for a total volume of 60 mL.
Gradually increase gradient from 0 to 40% buffer D over 50 mL.
From 50 mL, increase gradient from 40% to 100% over 1 mL.
At 70 mL, decrease gradient from 100% to 0% over 1 mL.
Stop the method at 90 mL.
Run SDS-PAGE of fractions containing UV peaks to identify relevant fractions.
Pool toxin-containing fractions and concentrate using a 5 mL Amicon column with a 30 kDa cutoff by spinning at 3500 × g for approximately 15 minutes at 4°C until the volume reaches 400–500 μL.
Equilibrate a Superdex 200 10/300GL increase column with buffer E.
Inject 0.5 mL of concentrated protein elute from HiTrap SP chromatography into AKTA sample loop.
Run ‘Size Ex −500 µL’ program: Set flow rate to 0.25 mL/min.
Fractionate at 0.5 mL intervals for a total volume of 28 mL.
Stop the method after processing 28 mL.
Assess toxin concentration and analyze on SDS-PAGE.
Transfer 1 mL of settled Pierce NHS-activated agarose resin and wash with PBS.
Incubate the washed resin with PBS containing 14 mg of TyTx1 antibody for 1 hour at 25°C with gentle rocking.
Wash the resin four times with 5 mL of PBS.
Quench the resin by repeated washing with 10 mL of 0.5 M Tris-HCl, pH 8.0.
Store the quenched resin at 4°C until use.
Culture E. coli BL21(DE3) harboring pET28a+ carrying tagless typhoid toxin subunits in LB to approximately OD600=0.7 at 37°C.
Transfer the culture to 28°C and add 0.5 mM IPTG.
Incubate for 16 hours.
Resuspend the harvested bacteria pellet in buffer E.
Subject the resuspended bacterial cells to three freeze-thaw cycles in liquid nitrogen.
Lysate the bacterial cells by sonication.
Centrifuge the lysed sample at 18,000 × g for 30 minutes at 4°C.
Mix the clarified lysate with TyTx1-conjugated agarose.
Incubate the mixture at 4°C for 30 minutes with gentle rocking.
Capture the resin by passing the mixture through a gravity column.
Wash the resin with buffer E.
Elute the protein using 5 mL of 100 mM Glycine, pH 3.0.
Neutralize the eluted protein immediately by adding 1 mL of 1 M Tris-HCl, pH 8.8.
Apply the purified protein to size exclusion chromatography.
Mix TyTx1 mAbs with wild-type purified typhoid toxin (PltB, PltA, CdtB) in a 1:1 ratio.
Incubate the antibody-toxin mixture at 4°C for at least 16 hours.
Submit the antibody-antigen complex to a Superdex 200 10/300 increase column using buffer F.
Collect fractions corresponding to the antibody-antigen complex.
Measure the concentrations using the Bradford solution.
Dilute IgG-toxin complex samples with buffer F to a final concentration of 0.1 mg/mL.
Dilute IgG-toxin complex samples with buffer F to a final concentration of 0.2 mg/mL.
Apply 3.5 μL of diluted sample to glow-discharged copper Quantifoil R1.2/1.3 300 mesh cryo-EM grid mounted on the Vitrobot.
Blot the applied sample using settings of Blot total – 1, Blot force – 1, and blot time – 2 to 4 seconds.
Drain the blot for 1 second.
Wait 0 seconds before plunge freezing in liquid ethane.
Plunge freeze the grid into liquid ethane.
Store frozen grids in liquid nitrogen until analysis.
Perform motion correction of each image stack using MotionCor2 function in RELION.
Subject the movies to Laplacian-of-Gaussian particle picking in RELION 3.
Manually pick approximately 1000 particles, extract them, and perform 2D classification for automated particle picking templates.
Extract 1,009,626 particles at 3.0457 Å/pixel to reduce memory requirements and speed up image processing.
Use the 2D classification results to remove incorrectly picked particles.
Generate an ab initio model from the cleaned particle set using CryoSparc 2.
Use the generated 3D ab initio model as a reference map for subsequent 3D classifications and refinement in RELION 3.
Perform initial 3D classification to reveal classes containing Fab-like structures.
Combine high-quality particles from identified classes for another round of 3D classification.
Identify one class with high-quality particles for high-resolution estimate modeling.
Use the refined particles from this class for subsequent per-particle CTF refinements and 3D refinement.
